questions.title: Atropine treats mushroom poisoning
questions.question: Indicate a drug which is effective in the treatment of mushroom (muscarine) poisoning:

explanations.A: Correct. Many poisonous mushrooms contain muscarine, a direct muscarinic agonist, and their toxicity produces a muscarinic-excess picture (salivation, lacrimation, GI cramping, bradycardia). Atropine, by competitively blocking the same muscarinic receptors, is the antidote of choice. It reverses the muscarinic-excess picture regardless of whether the excess acetylcholine-like stimulation comes from muscarine itself, a cholinesterase inhibitor, or a direct-acting cholinomimetic overdose.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pralidoxime reactivates acetylcholinesterase after organophosphate binding; it has no role in a direct muscarinic-agonist poisoning such as mushroom (muscarine) toxicity, where the enzyme itself is not inhibited.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Homatropine is itself an antimuscarinic mydriatic used ophthalmically, not the systemic antidote used for mushroom poisoning.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Diazepam is a benzodiazepine used for seizures or agitation; it does not antagonize the muscarinic-excess picture of mushroom poisoning.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Dicyclomine is itself an antimuscarinic antispasmodic, not the systemic antidote used for this specific indication.

questions.title: Mydriatic antimuscarinics
questions.question: Indicate the antimuscarinic drug which is used as a mydriatic:

explanations.A: Incorrect as the single best answer. Tropicamide genuinely is an antimuscarinic mydriatic, but so are cyclopentolate and homatropine, making "all of the above" the more complete answer.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the single best answer. Cyclopentolate genuinely is an antimuscarinic mydriatic, but so are tropicamide and homatropine, making "all of the above" the more complete answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect as the single best answer. Homatropine genuinely is an antimuscarinic mydriatic, but so are tropicamide and cyclopentolate, making "all of the above" the more complete answer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. All three listed drugs, not merely two, are antimuscarinic mydriatics.
explanations.E: Correct. Tropicamide, cyclopentolate and homatropine are all antimuscarinic mydriatics used in ophthalmic practice. Each blocks the muscarinic receptors on the iris sphincter (pupillae constrictor) muscle, relaxing it and letting the dilator muscle's unopposed sympathetic tone widen the pupil. They differ mainly in onset and duration (tropicamide is shortest-acting, homatropine intermediate, and atropine itself longest), but all three share this same mydriatic mechanism.

questions.title: Scopolamine's rapid, extensive CNS distribution
questions.question: Indicate the drug which is rapidly and fully distributed into the CNS and has a greater effect than most other antimuscarinic agents:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ipratropium is a charged quaternary antimuscarinic, poorly absorbed systemically and essentially excluded from the CNS, the opposite profile from the one this question describes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Oxybutynin does cross into the CNS to some degree at systemic doses, but it is not the antimuscarinic classically taught as being most rapidly and fully CNS-distributed.
explanations.C: Correct. Scopolamine (hyoscine) is a lipid-soluble tertiary amine that crosses into the CNS more readily and extensively than atropine or the other antimuscarinics listed, producing a more marked central effect (sedation, amnesia) at standard doses. This greater CNS penetration is exactly why scopolamine, rather than atropine, is preferred as a premedication for its calming, amnestic action and as a motion-sickness antiemetic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hyoscine butyl bromide is the quaternary (charged) derivative of hyoscine, deliberately modified so that it does NOT cross into the CNS, restricting it to peripheral antispasmodic use.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Homatropine is a peripherally- and ocularly-acting mydriatic; it is not characterised by the rapid, extensive CNS distribution this question tests.

questions.title: Glycopyrrolate has the least effect on pupil size
questions.question: It is an anticholinergic drug used in pre-anesthetic medication and has the LEAST effect on pupil size:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Tropicamide is itself a mydriatic; it produces, rather than spares, a pupil effect.
explanations.B: Correct. Glycopyrrolate is a charged quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic, and this charge excludes it from crossing into the eye, so it produces the least effect on pupil size among the pre-anesthetic antimuscarinic options. This is exactly why glycopyrrolate is chosen when the prescriber wants to dry secretions before anesthesia without also causing troublesome mydriasis, unlike the lipid-soluble tertiary amines atropine, homatropine and hyoscine.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Homatropine is itself a mydriatic; it produces, rather than spares, a pupil effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Atropine, a lipid-soluble tertiary amine, does produce mydriasis at systemic pre-anesthetic doses.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hyoscine, also a lipid-soluble tertiary amine, likewise produces a pupil effect at systemic pre-anesthetic doses.

questions.title: Atropine poisoning does not cause bradycardia
questions.question: Manifestations of atropine poisoning include all of the following symptoms EXCEPT:

options.B: Hyperthermia, dry mouth and hot skin

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cutaneous flushing genuinely is a feature of atropine poisoning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hyperthermia with dry, hot skin from inhibited sweating genuinely is a feature of atropine poisoning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. CNS excitation with agitation and delirium genuinely is a feature of atropine poisoning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mydriasis and cycloplegia genuinely are ocular features of atropine poisoning, so this is not the exception.
explanations.E: Correct. Atropine poisoning produces tachycardia, not bradycardia, because blocking vagal M2 tone on the SA node removes the parasympathetic brake on heart rate rather than slowing it. Orthostatic hypotension is likewise not a typical feature of atropine's own cardiovascular profile, since atropine's dominant cardiac action is chronotropic rather than a fall in blood pressure. Because this question asks for the exception, the false pairing of bradycardia and orthostatic hypotension is the one that does not belong among atropine poisoning's genuine manifestations.

questions.learning_objective: State that atropine poisoning produces tachycardia, not bradycardia, among its manifestations.

questions.title: Atropine's bronchodilator effect is not useful in acute pulmonary edema
questions.question: The bronchodilator effect of atropine or its substitutes is NOT useful in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Antimuscarinic bronchodilation genuinely is useful in COPD, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Antimuscarinic bronchodilation genuinely is useful in bronchial asthma, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Atropine's antisecretory/bronchodilator action genuinely is used in pre-anesthetic medication, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Correct. Acute pulmonary edema is a fluid-overload/cardiac problem, not a bronchospastic one, so an antimuscarinic bronchodilator does not address its underlying pathology. Management instead centers on diuretics, nitrates, and positive-pressure ventilation. Atropine's drying, tachycardia-inducing effects could even be counterproductive in this specific cardiac setting.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Antimuscarinic bronchodilation genuinely is useful in reflex bronchospasm, so this is not the exception.

questions.title: Atropine competitively blocks muscarinic excess
questions.question: The excessive stimulation of muscarinic receptors by pilocarpine and choline esters is blocked competitively by:

explanations.A: Correct. Atropine competitively antagonises the muscarinic receptor, so it displaces and blocks excess stimulation from a direct muscarinic agonist such as pilocarpine or a choline ester, regardless of the specific agonist responsible. This same competitive antagonism is the basis for using atropine as the antidote across the whole family of muscarinic-excess states, from direct agonist overdose to cholinesterase-inhibitor poisoning. Its action is reversible, so the degree of blockade depends on the relative concentrations of atropine and the agonist at the receptor.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Edrophonium is itself a cholinesterase inhibitor; it would increase, not block, muscarinic stimulation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pralidoxime reactivates organophosphate-inhibited acetylcholinesterase; it has no direct antagonist action at the muscarinic receptor itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Echothiophate is itself an irreversible cholinesterase inhibitor; it would increase, not block, muscarinic stimulation.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Diazepam is a benzodiazepine with no muscarinic receptor antagonist activity.

questions.learning_objective: State that atropine competitively blocks muscarinic-receptor overstimulation from direct agonists such as pilocarpine and choline esters.

questions.title: Scopolamine does not cause diaphoresis
questions.question: The following adverse effects would NOT be expected with scopolamine:

explanations.A: Correct. Scopolamine, like every antimuscarinic, blocks the muscarinic receptors on eccrine sweat glands, so it decreases rather than increases sweating. Diaphoresis (excess sweating) is therefore not an expected antimuscarinic adverse effect; if anything, antimuscarinic overdose tends toward hot, dry skin from impaired sweating rather than diaphoresis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Blurred vision, from cycloplegia (paralysis of accommodation), genuinely is an expected scopolamine adverse effect.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Constipation, from reduced GI motility, genuinely is an expected scopolamine adverse effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Confusion, from scopolamine's prominent CNS penetration, genuinely is an expected adverse effect.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Xerostomia (dry mouth), from blocked salivary gland secretion, genuinely is an expected antimuscarinic adverse effect.

questions.title: Atropine's mechanism is competitive muscarinic blockade
questions.question: The mechanism of atropine's action is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Atropine blocks muscarinic, not nicotinic, receptors.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Atropine blocks muscarinic, not nicotinic, receptors, and its blockade is competitive, not noncompetitive.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Atropine's muscarinic receptor blockade is competitive, not noncompetitive; it can be displaced by a sufficiently high concentration of agonist.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Atropine has no action at the nicotinic neuromuscular junction.
explanations.E: Correct. Atropine's single unifying mechanism across every tissue is competitive, reversible blockade of the muscarinic acetylcholine receptor. Because the blockade is competitive, atropine's effect can be overcome by a sufficiently high local concentration of acetylcholine or another muscarinic agonist, which is part of why atropine dosing must be titrated against the severity of a muscarinic-excess poisoning. This same single mechanism explains atropine's entire effect profile, from bronchodilation to mydriasis to antisecretory action.

questions.learning_objective: State that atropine acts by competitive muscarinic receptor blockade.

questions.title: Scopolamine resembles atropine
questions.question: The pharmacologic actions of scopolamine most closely resemble those of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Succinylcholine is a depolarising neuromuscular blocker acting at nicotinic receptors, an entirely different mechanism from scopolamine's muscarinic blockade.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Physostigmine is a cholinesterase inhibitor that increases, rather than blocks, muscarinic stimulation, the opposite action from scopolamine's.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hexamethonium is a ganglionic nicotinic blocker, a different receptor and site of action from scopolamine's peripheral/central muscarinic blockade.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pilocarpine is a direct-acting muscarinic agonist, the opposite action from scopolamine's antagonism.
explanations.E: Correct. Scopolamine and atropine are both naturally-occurring tropane belladonna alkaloids sharing the same competitive muscarinic-receptor-blocking mechanism, so their peripheral pharmacologic actions closely resemble one another. They differ mainly in their relative CNS penetration and resulting central effect profile, with scopolamine producing more prominent sedation, rather than in the fundamental mechanism itself.

questions.title: Neostigmine is not used to treat atropine poisoning
questions.question: Treatment of atropine poisoning does not include:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diazepam genuinely is used supportively to control agitation/delirium in atropine poisoning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Gastric lavage genuinely is a supportive measure to limit further absorption after oral atropine overdose, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cooling blankets genuinely are used supportively to manage atropine-poisoning hyperthermia, so they are not the exception.
explanations.D: Correct. Neostigmine is a charged quaternary cholinesterase inhibitor that is excluded from the CNS, so it cannot reach and reverse the central component of the atropine-poisoning toxidrome. Physostigmine, a lipid-soluble tertiary amine cholinesterase inhibitor that does cross the blood-brain barrier, is used instead precisely because it can antagonise both the peripheral and central effects of atropine toxicity.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Physostigmine, unlike neostigmine, genuinely is used to treat atropine poisoning because it crosses into the CNS, so it is not the exception.

questions.title: Vivid dreams are a famous scopolamine side effect
questions.question: Vivid dreams are a famous side effect of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Atropine's CNS penetration and central effect are less prominent than scopolamine's, and vivid dreams are not the side effect atropine is classically known for.

explanations.E: Incorrect. Neostigmine is a cholinesterase inhibitor, not an antimuscarinic, and its quaternary charge excludes it from the CNS regardless.

questions.title: Ipratropium bronchodilates via dry powder inhaler in COPD
questions.question: Which of the following agents is used to induce bronchodilation by a dry powder inhaler in COPD?

explanations.A: Correct. Ipratropium is the inhaled antimuscarinic bronchodilator used in COPD, particularly when a beta-2 agonist alone is not sufficient. Its charged quaternary structure keeps it largely confined to the airway after inhalation, minimising the systemic antimuscarinic side effects that would limit chronic use of systemic atropine for the same purpose.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lobeline is a nicotinic-receptor-active alkaloid historically explored as a smoking-cessation aid, not an inhaled antimuscarinic bronchodilator.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hyoscine is used for its antisecretory/antiemetic/sedative effects, not delivered as a dry powder inhaler for COPD bronchodilation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Atropine itself is not used as an inhaled COPD bronchodilator because its systemic antimuscarinic side-effect burden is unacceptable for chronic respiratory maintenance therapy.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Homatropine is an ophthalmic mydriatic, not an inhaled COPD bronchodilator.

questions.title: Pirenzepine is a selective M1 blocker
questions.question: Which of the following antimuscarinic drugs is a selective M1 blocker?

explanations.A: Incorrect as the single best answer here. This source's own key groups dicyclomine among the M1-selective agents alongside pirenzepine and trihexyphenidyl, making "all of the above" the intended complete answer, though dicyclomine is more commonly taught elsewhere as a non-selective antimuscarinic antispasmodic.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the single best answer here. This source's own key groups trihexyphenidyl among the M1-selective agents alongside pirenzepine and dicyclomine, making "all of the above" the intended complete answer, though trihexyphenidyl is more commonly taught elsewhere as a non-selective antiparkinsonian antimuscarinic.
explanations.C: Incorrect as the single best answer here. Pirenzepine genuinely is the prototype M1-selective muscarinic antagonist, but this source's printed key groups it with two further drugs rather than naming it alone.
explanations.D: Incorrect. All three listed drugs, per this source's printed key, are grouped as M1-selective, not merely two.
explanations.E: Correct per this source. Pirenzepine is the prototype M1-selective muscarinic receptor antagonist, historically used for peptic ulcer disease because gastric parietal-cell acid secretion is predominantly M1-mediated, letting it spare the cardiac (M2) and glandular/smooth-muscle (M3) effects a non-selective antimuscarinic would carry. This source's printed key extends that M1-selective classification to dicyclomine and trihexyphenidyl as well; standard pharmacology references more commonly teach pirenzepine (and telenzepine) alone as the classic M1-selective examples, a discrepancy the field_notes/uncertainty on this question's concept records rather than silently resolving.

questions.title: Bethanechol causes atropine-blockable vasodilation
questions.question: Which of the following drugs causes vasodilation that can be blocked by atropine?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cyclopentolate is an antimuscarinic mydriatic; as a muscarinic antagonist, it does not itself trigger a muscarinic vasodilator response.
explanations.B: Correct. Bethanechol is a direct-acting muscarinic agonist that stimulates M3 receptors on vascular endothelium, triggering nitric-oxide release and vasodilation, even though blood vessels themselves receive no direct parasympathetic innervation. Because this response is genuinely mediated through the muscarinic receptor, it is blocked by atropine, unlike a vasodilation produced through a non-muscarinic mechanism.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pralidoxime is a cholinesterase reactivator used in organophosphate poisoning; it has no direct vasodilator action of its own.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Nicotine acts at nicotinic, not muscarinic, receptors, so any vasomotor effect it produces is not blocked by the muscarinic antagonist atropine.

questions.title: Benztropine is used for Parkinson's disease
questions.question: Which of the following drugs is useful in the treatment of Parkinson's disease?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Succinylcholine is a depolarising neuromuscular blocker used for surgical/procedural paralysis, not a Parkinsonism treatment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Edrophonium is a short-acting cholinesterase inhibitor used diagnostically (historically for myasthenia gravis), not a Parkinsonism treatment.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Oxybutynin is an antimuscarinic used for overactive bladder, not specifically indicated for Parkinsonism.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hexamethonium is a ganglionic blocker with no role in Parkinsonism treatment.
explanations.E: Correct. Benztropine is a purpose-built centrally-acting antimuscarinic used specifically for Parkinsonism, restoring the dopaminergic/cholinergic balance in the striatum by blocking the relatively unopposed cholinergic activity that follows striatal dopamine loss. Atropine itself is not used for this indication, since a purpose-built antimuscarinic with a more favourable central selectivity profile, such as benztropine, is preferred.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Atropine is poorly absorbed after oral administration
options.B: Ipratropium is well absorbed with a long systemic action
options.C: Benztropine is a quaternary amine with poor CNS penetration
options.D: Cyclopentolate is well absorbed from the conjunctival sac into the systemic circulation

explanations.A: Incorrect. Atropine, a lipid-soluble tertiary amine, is well (not poorly) absorbed after oral administration.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ipratropium is a charged quaternary compound that is poorly absorbed systemically and has a short duration, deliberately confining its action largely to the airway after inhalation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Benztropine must cross the blood-brain barrier to treat Parkinsonism, so it is a lipid-soluble tertiary amine with good, not poor, CNS penetration, not a quaternary compound.
explanations.D: Correct. The conjunctival sac is a genuine absorptive surface, and cyclopentolate, like other topical antimuscarinic mydriatics, is well absorbed from it into the systemic circulation rather than staying confined to the eye. This systemic absorption is why topical ocular antimuscarinics can occasionally produce systemic antimuscarinic side effects, particularly in young children or when used repeatedly.

questions.title: Beta-2 receptors facilitate both lipolysis and glycogenolysis
questions.question: Choose the correct statement about epinephrine's metabolic effects:

options.A: Beta-2 receptors increase blood glucose by inducing liver and muscle glycogenolysis
options.B: Beta-2 receptors facilitate lipolysis and glycogenolysis
options.C: Alpha-1 receptors are the main receptors that mediate glycogenolysis
options.D: Alpha-2 receptors facilitate lipolysis and glycogenolysis

explanations.A: Incorrect as the single best answer. This statement is true as far as it goes, but it captures only the glycogenolysis/blood-glucose part of beta-2's metabolic profile and omits the lipolysis effect this question also tests, making option B the more complete statement.
explanations.B: Correct. Beta-2 receptor activation raises blood glucose by stimulating hepatic and skeletal-muscle glycogenolysis and separately facilitates lipolysis in adipose tissue, together producing the classic catecholamine metabolic signature of hyperglycemia and elevated free fatty acids. This is the more complete statement of beta-2's metabolic effects, covering both the carbohydrate and lipid sides of its action.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Beta, not alpha-1, receptors are the main mediators of glycogenolysis; alpha-1 receptors instead primarily mediate smooth-muscle contraction and other Gq-coupled effects.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Alpha-2 receptors inhibit, rather than facilitate, lipolysis, the opposite direction from this statement, consistent with alpha-2's Gi coupling.
explanations.E: Incorrect as the single best answer. Beta-1 receptors are primarily cardiac and juxtaglomerular in distribution; beta-2, not beta-1, is the receptor classically credited with mediating adipose-tissue lipolysis in this metabolic context.

questions.title: Norepinephrine's action ends mainly by presynaptic reuptake
questions.question: Termination of norepinephrine's effect is MAINLY due to:

options.C: Diffusion of norepinephrine away from receptors

explanations.A: Incorrect as the main mechanism. Catechol-O-methyltransferase does metabolise norepinephrine, but this is a secondary clearance pathway, not the main termination mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. Norepinephrine's synaptic action is terminated mainly by active reuptake into the presynaptic nerve terminal (uptake 1), the same transporter that drugs such as cocaine and tricyclic antidepressants block to potentiate noradrenergic transmission. Enzymatic metabolism by COMT and MAO acts as a secondary clearance mechanism rather than the dominant termination pathway.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Passive diffusion away from the receptor is not the main termination mechanism for a synaptic transmitter with an active, high-affinity reuptake transporter available.
explanations.D: Incorrect as the main mechanism. Monoamine oxidase does metabolise norepinephrine, but this is a secondary clearance pathway, not the main termination mechanism.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Norepinephrine is not a substrate for plasma esterase hydrolysis; that clearance route is more relevant to ester-linked drugs such as succinylcholine or esmolol.

questions.title: Bronchial, ciliary and pupillary-constrictor muscle lack alpha receptors
questions.question: Which of the following smooth muscles do not contain alpha receptors?

explanations.A: Incorrect as the single best answer. Bronchial smooth muscle genuinely lacks alpha receptors, but so do the ciliary and constrictor pupillae muscles, making "all of the above" the more complete answer.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the single best answer. The ciliary muscle genuinely lacks alpha receptors, but so do bronchial smooth muscle and the constrictor pupillae muscle, making "all of the above" the more complete answer.

questions.title: Norepinephrine from sympathetic nerves, epinephrine from the adrenal medulla
questions.question: The most important catecholamine secreted by sympathetic nerves is ________, while that secreted by the adrenal medulla is ________:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Norepinephrine genuinely is the main sympathetic-nerve catecholamine, but dopamine is not the main adrenal-medullary secretion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Dopamine is not the main sympathetic-nerve catecholamine; norepinephrine is.
explanations.C: Correct. Norepinephrine is the principal transmitter released by postganglionic sympathetic nerve terminals, while epinephrine is instead the main catecholamine secreted by the adrenal medulla's chromaffin cells, which express the extra enzyme (phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase) needed to N-methylate norepinephrine into epinephrine. This division -- norepinephrine for direct neural sympathetic transmission, epinephrine as the adrenal hormone -- is a foundational distinction in autonomic pharmacology.

questions.title: Presynaptic alpha-2 autoreceptors are stimulated by norepinephrine
questions.question: The presynaptic receptor that is stimulated by norepinephrine is:

questions.title: Tyrosine hydroxylase is rate-limiting for catecholamine synthesis
questions.question: The rate-limiting step in catecholamine biosynthesis is catalyzed by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase catalyses the final step (norepinephrine to epinephrine) in the adrenal medulla, not the pathway's rate-limiting step.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Catechol-O-methyltransferase is a catecholamine-metabolising (breakdown) enzyme, not a biosynthetic enzyme.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dopa decarboxylase converts L-DOPA to dopamine, a step downstream of the pathway's rate-limiting step.
explanations.D: Correct. Tyrosine hydroxylase, which converts tyrosine to L-DOPA, catalyzes the rate-limiting step of catecholamine biosynthesis, upstream of dopamine, norepinephrine and epinephrine formation. Because it is rate-limiting, its activity (regulated by feedback inhibition from the pathway's own end-products) determines the overall rate of catecholamine production.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Dopamine beta-hydroxylase converts dopamine to norepinephrine, a step downstream of the pathway's rate-limiting step.

options.A: Both types of MAO inhibitor are used for treatment of depression
options.B: Selective MAO-B inhibitor is used for treatment of depression while selective MAO-A inhibitor is used for treatment of Parkinsonism
options.C: Both types of MAO inhibitor are used for treatment of Parkinsonism

questions.title: Epinephrine reversal occurs with phentolamine pretreatment
questions.question: "Epinephrine reversal" could occur if epinephrine is administered in the presence of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cocaine blocks norepinephrine reuptake, potentiating rather than reversing epinephrine's pressor effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Propranolol is a nonselective beta-blocker; blocking beta-2 vasodilation while leaving alpha-1 vasoconstriction intact would leave epinephrine's pressor effect unopposed or even exaggerated, not reversed.
explanations.C: Correct. Pretreating with an alpha-adrenergic blocker such as phentolamine produces the classic epinephrine-reversal phenomenon: with alpha-1 vasoconstriction blocked, epinephrine's unopposed beta-2 vasodilation dominates, so blood pressure falls instead of rising. This is the textbook demonstration that epinephrine's net pressor effect depends on which receptor's action is left unopposed.

questions.title: Alpha-methyldopa does not bind alpha-2 receptors directly
questions.question: All of the following bind selectively to alpha-2 receptors EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Yohimbine genuinely binds alpha-2 receptors directly (as an antagonist), so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Clonidine genuinely binds alpha-2 receptors directly (as an agonist), so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Correct. Alpha-methyldopa is a prodrug, not an active alpha-2 ligand in its own right. It must first be metabolized to alpha-methylnorepinephrine, and only that active metabolite can then act at the alpha-2 receptor. questions.question: Which amphetamine-related CNS stimulant lacks abuse potential?

questions.title: Dobutamine is not preferred to isoprenaline in heart block
questions.question: Choose the incorrect statement about dobutamine:

options.B: Is useful as short-term inotropic support
options.C: Is given only by IV infusion
options.E: Is preferred to isoprenaline in heart block

explanations.A: Incorrect as the answer -- this statement is true. Dobutamine genuinely is a selective beta-1 agonist, so it is not the false statement this question asks for.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the answer -- this statement is true. Dobutamine genuinely is used as short-term inotropic support, so it is not the false statement this question asks for.
explanations.C: Incorrect as the answer -- this statement is true. Dobutamine, as a catecholamine destroyed by first-pass metabolism, genuinely must be given by IV infusion, so it is not the false statement this question asks for.
explanations.D: Incorrect as the answer -- this statement is true. Dobutamine's inotropic/chronotropic effect genuinely can increase myocardial oxygen demand and induce angina pain, so it is not the false statement this question asks for.
explanations.E: Correct (this is the FALSE statement, and so the correct answer to an incorrect-statement question). Dobutamine's selective beta-1 agonism gives it a strong inotropic but only minimally chronotropic effect, unlike isoprenaline's strong, nonselective beta agonism, which produces the more pronounced chronotropic drive needed to raise heart rate in complete heart block. Isoprenaline, not dobutamine, is therefore preferred specifically for heart block, making the claim that dobutamine is preferred to isoprenaline in that setting the false statement.

questions.title: Epinephrine is first-line for anaphylactic shock
questions.question: Epinephrine is the life-saving, first-line treatment in:

explanations.A: Correct. Epinephrine is the life-saving, first-line drug for anaphylactic shock. It acts through combined alpha-1 (vasoconstriction, reducing mucosal edema and hypotension), beta-1 (cardiac support) and beta-2 (bronchodilation) effects that together reverse the anaphylactic picture faster than any single-receptor alternative. No other drug matches this combined, rapid-onset receptor profile, which is why epinephrine, not an antihistamine or corticosteroid, is given first.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the single best answer here. Epinephrine does have a role in cardiac arrest resuscitation protocols, but anaphylactic shock is the classic, most specific "life-saving first-line" indication this question tests.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Epinephrine is not the first-line treatment for epistaxis, which is instead managed with local pressure, packing or topical vasoconstrictors as needed.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Epinephrine is not used for acute (angle-closure) glaucoma; its mydriatic tendency could even worsen angle closure, and acute glaucoma is instead managed with agents that lower intraocular pressure and constrict the pupil.
explanations.E: Incorrect as the single best answer here. A beta-2 agonist, not epinephrine, is the first-line bronchodilator for routine bronchial asthma; epinephrine's own first-line role is specifically in anaphylactic shock.

questions.learning_objective: State that epinephrine is the life-saving, first-line drug for anaphylactic shock.
